title: Queue integrity: pending count, ordering and aging match the underlying records
risk: The dashboard badge and the approval queue disagree, so items silently age past their TTL or operators work on a stale list.
preconditions: Namespace gov-apv-<case_id>-<worker_id>; approval queue seeded from fixtures/offline/governance.json.
Operator identities and roles resolved from the fixture operator registry; every decision goes through POST /api/v1/approvals/{id}/decision, the only approval route.
Three items exist for T1: one pending within TTL, one pending close to TTL, one expired. T2 has one pending item.

steps.action: Fetch the T1 approval queue and the SCR-001 approval_pending indicator
steps.expected: Both report the same actionable count (2) and the expired item is excluded or explicitly marked expired, not counted as actionable.
Items are ordered by expiry ascending so the soonest-to-expire appears first.

steps.action: Fetch the T1 queue again as an operator and confirm tenant scoping
steps.expected: No T2 item appears in the T1 listing.

steps.action: Drive the clock past the second item's expiry and refresh
steps.expected: The actionable count drops to 1 and the newly expired item is shown as expired rather than disappearing without trace.

assertions: Dashboard indicator and queue listing derive from the same records: counts agree exactly (2, then 1).
Expired items never count as actionable but remain visible with a terminal marker.
Ordering is deterministic by expiry so the most urgent item is first.
Tenant scoping is exact: zero foreign items in the listing.
forbidden: Computing the badge from a different query than the list.
Hiding expired items so aging is invisible.
Including another tenant's items to inflate the queue.
evidence: Queue payload and SCR-001 indicator values at both clock points.
cleanup: Delete gov- approval rows after export.
automation: Real queue query and dashboard projection under test; the clock is injected so aging is deterministic and both surfaces are read from live queries rather than cached copies.
note: Generated acceptance specification. Plain specification, not an executable test; no application runtime exists, so the status is NOT_RUN.
